s1.syndrome_frame: Acute unilateral vision loss with eye pain and signs of intraocular inflammation
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
Anterior chamber cells and fibrin
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
Decline in visual acuity with development of hypopyon
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
Anterior chamber had 3+ cells with fibrin
Mild nuclear sclerosis and a whitish focal granuloma at the 4-o'clock position
Posterior segment was unremarkable
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius
Blood and urine cultures, electrocardiogram, and echocardiogram were unremarkable

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of gram-positive cocci and rods, and positive culture for Streptococcus intermedius, suggest bacterial endophthalmitis

shortlist.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Specific identification of Streptococcus intermedius in culture points to this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Intraocular inflammation and signs of uveitis, such as keratic precipitates and cells in the anterior chamber

shortlist.label: Iritis
shortlist.why_kept: Focal granuloma at the pupillary margin and signs of inflammation in the anterior chamber

shortlist.label: Iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body, consistent with the patient's symptoms and examination findings

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, toxoplasmosis can cause uveitis and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Sympathetic ophthalmia
shortlist.why_kept: A rare but potentially devastating condition that can occur after penetrating eye injury or surgery, and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Gram-positive bacterial endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of gram-positive bacteria in the Gram stain and positive culture for Streptococcus intermedius support this diagnosis
